title: At Bogyoke Market
title_target: ဗိုလ်ချုပ်ဈေး မှာ — boh-chohk-zay: hma
goal: Buy things by saying how many you want — and learn the Burmese way of counting: noun, then number, then a classifier, the opposite of English "five limes".
bekal: give quantities as noun — number — classifier
choose the classifiers ခု, လုံး, ယောက်, ခွက်, and စီး
ask how many with ဘယ်နှစ်…လဲ
ask for something with …ပေးပါ

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Buying fruit and a longyi
dialogs.intro: Ani goes to Bogyoke Market with Mya Mya. Watch how each request is built: the thing first, then the number, then the classifier. Read the literal lines and compare them with English "five limes" — the order is completely reversed.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဒီမှာ|dee-hma] [သစ်သီး|thik-thee:] [တွေ|dway] [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ဘာ|ba] [ဝယ်|wè] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: The fruit here is good. What do you want to buy?
lines.literal: here-at — fruit — (plural) — good — polite-statement. what — buy — want — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [သံပုရာသီး|thaⁿ-ba.ya-dhee:] [ငါး|nga:] [လုံး|lohⁿ:] [နဲ့|nè.] [ငှက်ပျောသီး|hngèk-pyò:-dhee:] [တစ်|ta.] [ဖီး|hpee:] [ပေး|pay:] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Five limes and a bunch of bananas, please.
lines.literal: lime — five — (round) — and — banana — one — (bunch) — give — polite.

lines.speaker: သည်သည်:
lines.text: [ရ|ya.] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [နှစ်ထောင်|hna.htowⁿ] [ပါ|ba] [ဒေါ်ဒေါ်|dò-dò]။

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဒီ|dee] [မန်ကျည်းသီး|maⁿ-chee:-dhee:] [ရော|yò:]။ [တစ်|ta.] [ပိဿာ|payk-tha] [ဘယ်လောက်|bè-lowk] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: And these tamarinds? How much for a viss?
lines.literal: this — tamarind — how about? one — viss — how-much — Q?

lines.speaker: သည်သည်:
lines.text: [တစ်ပိဿာ|ta.payk-tha] [သုံးထောင်|thohⁿ:-htowⁿ] [ပါ|ba]။ [ချို|hchoh] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]၊ [မြည်း|myee:] [ကြည့်|chee.] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Three thousand a viss. They're sweet — have a taste.
lines.literal: one-viss — three-thousand — polite. sweet — polite-statement, taste — see — polite.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [အင်း|iⁿ:]၊ [ချို|hchoh] [တယ်|dè]။ [တစ်ပိဿာ|ta.payk-tha] [ယူ|yoo] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: Mmm, they're sweet. I'll take one viss.
lines.literal: mmm, sweet — statement. one-viss — take — will.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [အာနီ|a-nee]၊ [ထဘီ|hta.mayⁿ] [ဝယ်|wè] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [လား|la:]။ [ဟိုမှာ|hoh-hma] [ဆိုင်|hsaiⁿ] [ရှိ|shee.] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Ani, do you want to buy a longyi? There's a shop over there.
lines.literal: ani, longyi — buy — want — Q? there-at — shop — exist — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဝယ်|wè] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [တစ်ထည်|ta.htè] [ဘယ်လောက်|bè-lowk] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Yes, I do. How much is one?
lines.literal: buy — want — polite-statement. one-(garment) — how-much — Q?

lines.speaker: ဆိုင်ရှင်:
lines.text: [တစ်ထည်|ta.htè] [တစ်သောင်း|ta.thowⁿ:] [ပါ|ba]။ [နှစ်ထည်|hna.htè] [ဆို|hsoh] [တစ်သောင်း|ta.thowⁿ:] [ရှစ်ထောင်|shik-htowⁿ] [ပေး|pay:] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Ten thousand each. If you take two, just give me eighteen thousand.
lines.literal: one-(garment) — ten-thousand — polite. two-(garment) — if — ten-thousand — eight-thousand — give — polite.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [နည်းနည်း|nè:-nè:] [လျှော့|shaw.] [ပါ|ba] [ဦး|ohⁿ:]။ [တစ်သောင်း|ta.thowⁿ:] [ငါးထောင်|nga:-htowⁿ] [ရ|ya.] [မလား|ma.la:]။
lines.id: Knock a little off, please. Can I have them for fifteen thousand?
lines.literal: little — reduce — polite — more. ten-thousand — five-thousand — OK — will-Q?

lines.speaker: ဆိုင်ရှင်:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [ရ|ya.] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ဘယ်|bè] [အရောင်|a.yowⁿ] [တွေ|dway] [ယူ|yoo] [မ|ma.] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: All right, you can. Which colors would you like?
lines.literal: true-yes, OK — polite-statement. which — color — (plural) — take — will — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [အပြာ|a.pya] [တစ်ထည်|ta.htè] [နဲ့|nè.] [အစိမ်း|a.sayⁿ:] [တစ်ထည်|ta.htè] [ပေး|pay:] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: One blue and one green, please.
lines.literal: blue — one-(garment) — and — green — one-(garment) — give — polite.

grammars.title: Noun — number — classifier: the Burmese counting order
body: This is the part of Burmese grammar that most needs rewiring for English speakers. We say "five limes"; Burmese says သံပုရာသီး ငါး လုံး — **noun, number, classifier**: "lime five round-thing". English does have a trace of this in "a **bunch** of bananas" or "two **cups** of tea", but Burmese uses it every single time.

head: English
Burmese
Say it
rows: စာအုပ် သုံး အုပ်
လူ နှစ် ယောက်
a cup of tea (tea one cup)
လက်ဖက်ရည် တစ် ခွက်
ကား တစ် စီး

after: Drill it by **reading the English backwards**: "five limes" → "lime five", then add the classifier. After a week the Burmese order starts to feel natural, and the classifier becomes the part you reach for automatically — just as you'd never say "two breads" instead of "two loaves of bread".

grammars.title: The classifiers you'll actually use
body: Burmese has dozens of classifiers, but A1 only needs about ten. If you really forget, use **ခု** (*hkoo.*) — it's for things in general and almost never sounds wrong.

head: Classifier
Say it
Used for
Example
rows: things in general — the safe choice
အိတ် နှစ်ခု
စာအုပ် ငါးအုပ်
ကော်ဖီ တစ်ခွက်
ကား နှစ်စီး
ကြောင် တစ်ကောင်
ထဘီ တစ်ထည်

after: ⚠️ Remember the sound change of numbers before a classifier: တစ် becomes *ta.* and နှစ် becomes *hna.*. So တစ်ခု is read *ta.hkoo.* and နှစ်ခွက် is read *hna.hkwèk*. You met this in unit 4, and it applies to every classifier without exception.

grammars.title: …ပေးပါ — asking politely
body: To ask for something, use the verb ပေး ("give") plus ပါ. The order: the thing, the amount, then ပေးပါ at the end — the verb stays in its usual place.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ရေ တစ်ပုလင်း ပေးပါ
ကော်ဖီ နှစ်ခွက် ပေးပါ

after: ဦး (*ohⁿ:*) at the end of a request means "a bit more, just this once" and makes your request sound coaxing rather than demanding. It's practically required when bargaining — without ဦး, ကျေးဇူးပြု၍ လျှော့ပါ sounds like an order.

grammars.title: Colors
body: Color words are formed with the prefix အ (*a.*) before the root. They can stand on their own as nouns — "a blue one" — just as in the dialogue: အပြာ တစ်ထည်, "blue, one garment".

head: Burmese
Say it
Color
Example
rows: အနီ တစ်ထည်

after: ⚠️ Notice that **အနီ** (red) sounds almost the same as our character's name, အာနီ (Ani) — the only difference is the length and tone of the first vowel. A good example of why length and tone matter in Burmese.

blocks.text: Bogyoke Aung San Market in Yangon is a covered market from the colonial era, and together with the small markets in every neighborhood it's still where most people shop. A few things work differently from what you may be used to.

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: viss, a unit of weight equal to 1.63 kg
small unit of weight, for gold and spices

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three things to know before you bargain
items: **Weight is measured in ပိဿာ (viss), not kilograms.** One viss is about 1.6 kg. If you ask for "a kilo", many sellers will understand, but the price they quote still refers to a viss — ask clearly: တစ်ပိဿာ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။
**Bargain with a smile, not a serious face.** Going down by a tenth to a fifth of the first price is considered fair; offering half is considered rude and usually ends the conversation.

**The first customer of the morning is called ဖွင့်ဈေး** (*hpwiⁿ.-zay:*, "the opening sale"), and many sellers give a special price because it's believed to bring luck for the whole day. Coming early has its perks.

It's a bit expensive — knock a little off, please.

ဘာ ဝယ်ချင်လဲ။ — တစ်ပိဿာ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။ — ကော်ဖီ နှစ်ခွက် ပေးပါ။ — နည်းနည်း ဈေးကြီးတယ်၊ လျှော့ပါဦး။ — အပြာ ယူပါ့မယ်။ — ဘယ်အရောင်တွေ ရှိလဲ။
